title: EXP-044 — Hello World Part 2: FX_UMs Table and IDO Creation Using FX_UMBase
objective: In the authenticated DEM configuration, follow docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt2.md at 04:08–05:16, adapted to factory-owned FX_ names, to determine whether the New Data Maintenance wizard can use the existing FX_UMBase property class and, only if that prerequisite and a separate target-name collision gate pass, create exactly one tenant-wide SQL table and corresponding IDO named FX_UMs in the existing FX_HelloWorldProject01 project, with Table Alias fxum. Configure FX_UM using property class FX_UMBase, mark it Primary Key and Required, and verify the Data Type, Length, and Label String ID inherited from that class. Configure FX_Description as String, Length 50, Label String ID FX_sDescription as a reference only. Perform at most one wizard Finish, decline optional Form creation, inspect the resulting objects, perform at most one ordinary lifecycle completion action on the newly created FX_UMs IDO if its observed state requires it, and verify the resulting table and IDO after ordinary close/reopen. Record decisive UI evidence, operation counts, cleanup ownership, and limitations. Classify findings as observed only.

in_scope: Before browser actions, read AGENTS.md, docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt2.md at 04:08–05:16, the accepted EXP-043 record and decisive evidence, and the relevant EXP-040 wizard creation, field-grid, Finish, IDO lifecycle, SQL Tables inspection, and recovery evidence. Consult EXP-039 only for the existing IDO project identity.

Use the existing authenticated DEM configuration G6R8LJ9Q4E8C2Z8Y_MONGOOSE_DEM_DEFAULT and Site Developer context. The surrounding Designer editing scope is User, but the intended SQL table and IDO are tenant-wide metadata, not User-scoped Form versions. Record this distinction explicitly.

Capture the initial browser state, active configuration, existing tabs, dialogs, pending edits, and repository baseline. Preserve the existing FX_UMBase property class, FX_HelloWorldProject01 project, FX_HelloWorld01 objects, and unrelated data.

T1 is a read-only prerequisite gate. Open the supported Web Designer New Form Definition route, select New Data and Maintenance through the visible UI, and inspect the New Data Maintenance wizard's Property Class list for FX_UMBase. Enter no values unless a prerequisite field is required to reach the relevant field grid or lookup; any such entry must remain uncommitted and be documented.

For T1, inspect the supported Property Class dropdown or lookup using visible options and supported lookup filtering. Capture the actual lookup criteria, exact matching row, displayed property-class identity, and whether selection is possible. Do not infer availability from the existing Property Classes maintenance Form alone.

If FX_UMBase is absent, unavailable, ambiguous, or cannot be conclusively found within the permitted recovery allowance, capture the decisive evidence, ordinarily Cancel the wizard using a freshly verified control, confirm no object was created, document the blocker, and stop the experiment. Do not attempt another metadata visibility mechanism.

If FX_UMBase is visibly available in T1, record the successful prerequisite gate, ordinarily Cancel the inspection wizard without Finish or persistent mutation, verify it is closed, and stop T1 for coordinator review. A later authorized task may reopen the wizard for the actual creation sequence.

Before the creation-stage Finish, use the existing IDOs and SQL Tables runtime Forms to establish zero existing FX_UMs targets in both collections. Use supported Filter-in-Place criteria and known-existing positive controls in each collection. Distinguish an unsaved blank placeholder from an actual data row. Check case-insensitive variants where the supported UI permits and do not claim coverage that has not been demonstrated. Stop before mutation on any collision or inconclusive result.

For SQL Tables inspection, use only the table grid's Filter-in-Place criteria row and supported execution controls, following the correction documented in EXP-040. Avoid entering criteria into an existing table's editable definition fields.
Before committing, verify that the existing project FX_HelloWorldProject01 is available for selection and that the intended target table and IDO names remain collision-free.

After both gates pass and a later task authorizes creation, open the New Data Maintenance wizard and configure exactly one Name FX_UMs, Project FX_HelloWorldProject01, and Table Alias fxum. Verify each visible field value after committing its editor.

In the wizard field grid, identify any initial blank row 1. If it is the same disposable new-wizard placeholder observed in EXP-040, remove that row exactly once using its supported row control, and verify that no configured or existing property is removed. If row identity is ambiguous, stop.

Configure the first intended field as FX_UM and select the visible FX_UMBase property class. Verify that the wizard displays the inherited Data Type String, Length 10, and Label String ID FX_sUM. Record any inherited Column Data Type value if the wizard exposes it. Set Primary Key and Required through their supported visible controls and verify both settings.

Configure the second intended field as FX_Description with Data Type String, Length 50, and Label String ID FX_sDescription. Treat FX_sDescription strictly as a reference; no string resource is to be created. Verify the resulting field grid contains exactly the two intended user-defined fields.

For ordinary wizard Name, text, and editable combobox fields, use one plain fill without slowly, followed by one separate Tab to commit and a fresh snapshot to verify. Use visible dropdown selection where the control requires selection rather than free text.

Use the established native Control+a, clear, and individual key-event typing procedure for the Web Client Select Form Name filter. Use supported visible Filter-in-Place input methods for runtime collection queries.

Capture all wizard pages and the fully configured final page before Finish, including project, target name, alias, property-class selection, inherited attributes, field cardinality, and key/required settings.

Invoke Finish exactly once only after the complete final wizard configuration and both prerequisite gates have been verified. Capture the exact immediate response and settled result. Do not retry an uncertain Finish.

If the wizard offers optional Create Form creation, obtain a fresh accessibility snapshot, identify the exact No control, activate No once, and verify that no Form creation proceeds. Stop on any unexpected or ambiguous prompt.

After successful creation, inspect FX_UMs in the existing IDOs maintenance Form under project FX_HelloWorldProject01. Verify exactly one intended IDO and inspect its base table, alias, properties, inherited FX_UMBase association, data types, lengths, and key/required settings.

Inspect the newly created FX_UMs IDO's ownership and lifecycle state. If it is visibly checked out, permit at most one ordinary check-in confined strictly to FX_UMs using a freshly verified supported control. Capture the exact response and resulting revision/ownership state. If already checked in, perform no lifecycle action. Never perform this operation on FX_UMBase or any pre-existing IDO.

Inspect the FX_UMs SQL table through the supported SQL Tables grid. Verify the displayed table identity, FX_UM as nvarchar(10) with primary-key and NOT NULL characteristics, and FX_Description as nvarchar(50). Record any additional system-generated columns separately from the two intended user-defined fields.

After clean post-creation inspection, ordinarily close the relevant IDOs and SQL Tables runtime Forms, recording each Form-tab removal and absence of unsaved-change prompts. Reopen each through supported Select Form navigation and perform exact-name collection queries for FX_UMs.

Compare the recovered IDO project, name, base table, alias, properties, property-class association, data types, lengths, and key/required settings against the post-creation baseline. Compare recovered SQL table columns, types, lengths, nullability, and primary-key identity against the post-creation SQL Tables baseline.
Permit at most one dismissal of an obstructing portal notification using only a freshly verified close x control. Never open notification links.

Before acting on any prompt, capture a fresh snapshot and verify the exact accessible button label and reference. Stop rather than automatically accepting validation, overwrite, discard, or unexpected confirmation prompts.
Use at most one fresh recovery snapshot and one corrected visible inspection following an interaction failure. If the required postcondition is still unresolved, stop and document the blocker.

Save screenshots, accessibility observations, exact lookup results, operation counts, errors, recovery accounting, and decisive acceptance evidence under evidence/EXP-044/. Record created-object ownership and cleanup responsibility in evidence/EXP-044/cleanup-inventory.md.

Confine repository edits to the EXP-044 experiment record and evidence/EXP-044/. Preserve pre-existing unrelated repository modifications. Perform a final evidence-content review and acceptance reconciliation without inventing proof from filenames.
Leave successfully created FX_UMs objects intact at the end of the experiment. Classify any successful single-run outcome as observed, not replay_verified.

acceptance_checks.description: Preflight evidence under evidence/EXP-044/ identifies the authenticated DEM configuration, usable Web Client and Designer, initial browser/Form state, existing FX_UMBase and FX_HelloWorldProject01 prerequisite identities, intended tenant-wide object scope, and repository baseline. No unintended mutation or session-establishment action occurs.

The first browser task reaches the supported New Data Maintenance wizard's Property Class lookup and records whether FX_UMBase is actually offered. A passing gate requires an exact visible FX_UMBase lookup result with unambiguous selection identity and a screenshot/accessibility observation. The inspection wizard is then cancelled without Finish or object creation. If the option is absent or cannot be verified, AC-2 fails, the experiment stops, and no subsequent creation action is authorized.

Before any Finish, supported read-only collection-query evidence establishes zero FX_UMs IDO records and zero FX_UMs SQL table records in their respective queried collections. Each query is accompanied by a known-existing positive control proving that the relevant filter executes. Case-insensitive coverage is demonstrated where available, or its limitation is explicitly recorded. Any collision or inconclusive absence result fails the creation gate.

Wizard evidence before Finish shows exactly one intended target Name FX_UMs, the selected existing project FX_HelloWorldProject01, and Table Alias fxum. Any initial blank field row has been verified and removed at most once without deleting a configured field. The final field grid contains exactly FX_UM and FX_Description as its intended user-defined fields.

Pre-Finish screenshots and accessibility snapshots show FX_UM selecting property class FX_UMBase, its displayed inherited Data Type String, Length 10, and Label String ID FX_sUM, with Primary Key and Required enabled. FX_Description shows Data Type String, Length 50, and Label String ID FX_sDescription. The exact displayed values and checked states are recorded before Finish.

Exactly one wizard Finish is recorded after AC-2 through AC-5 pass. The resulting UI displays an unambiguous successful creation response, without an unresolved validation or duplicate-name error. Any optional Create Form prompt is answered with a freshly verified No, and no Form is created. The Finish count, prompt response, and resulting state are captured.

One supported post-creation exact-name query in IDOs returns exactly one FX_UMs IDO in FX_HelloWorldProject01. The visible definition identifies the intended base table and alias fxum and exposes FX_UM and FX_Description with their configured Data Type, Length, key/required settings, and the FX_UMBase property-class association. Evidence identifies the actual IDO definition, not merely a selected list row.

The FX_UMs IDO ownership/lifecycle state is visibly captured. If the newly created IDO is checked out, exactly one permitted ordinary check-in is performed on FX_UMs and the settled revision/ownership result is verified. If already checked in, no such action occurs. Evidence confirms that no existing property class, IDO, or project was subjected to a lifecycle mutation.

A supported SQL Tables exact-name query returns exactly one dbo.FX_UMs table. The displayed table definition establishes FX_UM as nvarchar(10), NOT NULL, and primary key, and FX_Description as nvarchar(50). Any displayed system-generated columns or indexes are distinguished from the two authorized user-defined columns. The exact table identity and column definitions are captured in decisive evidence.

After clean ordinary closure of the relevant IDOs and SQL Tables runtime Forms, screenshots or snapshots show their Form tabs removed without unsaved-change prompts. Each is reopened through supported Select Form navigation and queried by exact target name. One recovered FX_UMs IDO and one recovered dbo.FX_UMs table match their respective AC-7 and AC-9 post-creation baselines, including the FX_UMBase property-class association where the IDO UI exposes it. This establishes same-session UI recovery only.

The cleanup inventory records the two created FX_UMs objects, their shared tenant-wide scope, project and alias, both field definitions, retained references, creation ownership, cleanup responsibility, observed lifecycle state, and confirmation that no cleanup was performed. Existing FX_UMBase, FX_HelloWorldProject01, and FX_HelloWorld01 objects are recorded as unchanged.

The final experiment record reconciles AC-1 through AC-11 against inspected screenshots, accessibility observations, and exact evidence paths; records all Finish, Save, close, reopen, lifecycle, and mutation counts; accounts for errors, prompts and recovery; audits repository confinement; and states the last verified browser state. Findings are classified observed or unresolved as supported, never replay_verified. No database durability, cross-session, or cross-user visibility claim is made.

initial_instruction: T1 — EXP-044 read-only wizard Property Class availability gate only. Before browser actions, read AGENTS.md, docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt2.md at 04:08–05:16, the decisive EXP-043 property-class creation/recovery evidence, and the relevant EXP-040 wizard route and field-grid evidence. Establish the repository baseline. Preflight the existing authenticated DEM Web Client and Designer without login, refresh, or session replacement. Preserve all existing tabs, records, and metadata. Through the supported visible Designer New Form Definition route, select New Data then Maintenance, and open the New Data Maintenance wizard. Navigate only as far as necessary to inspect the supported Property Class lookup. Do not create or save any object. Do not enter a target name or other wizard values unless a prerequisite entry is strictly necessary to reach the field grid; document any temporary uncommitted entry. Inspect the visible Property Class options and use only supported visible lookup filtering to determine whether FX_UMBase is offered. Capture the exact criteria, option text, target identity, settled UI state, screenshots, and accessibility observations. If FX_UMBase is not offered or the lookup cannot be conclusively inspected, use a freshly verified Cancel control to dismiss the wizard, verify no object was created, document the blocker, and STOP. Do not change FX_UMBase, invoke any metadata visibility mechanism, substitute a plain String type, or continue to table creation. If FX_UMBase is offered, capture decisive positive evidence, ordinarily Cancel the inspection wizard without Finish, verify no object was created, record the gate as passed, and STOP for coordinator review. Do not run the collision gate or begin FX_UMs creation in T1. Allow at most one fresh recovery snapshot and one corrected visible inspection after an interaction failure; stop if unresolved. Write only the EXP-044 experiment record and evidence/EXP-044/ files. Report exact observations, evidence contents and limitations, operation counts, recovery accounting, repository confinement, and final browser state. The complete workflow is proposed only; this T1 instruction must not commit any tenant-wide object.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261010-193233-I3F2. Rationale: EXP-043 was accepted at the observed same-session Web Client level: the FX_UMBase property class was saved with Data Type String, Length 10, Column Data Type nvarchar, and Label String ID FX_sUM, then recovered unchanged after ordinary close/reopen. However, the property class remains owned and locked by the current user, has not been checked in, and no metadata cache unload was performed. Its availability to the New Data Maintenance wizard is therefore unknown. EXP-040 established an observed wizard procedure for creating a coupled SQL table and IDO, including deletion of the initial blank field row, a single Finish, declining optional Form creation, and post-creation inspection. EXP-044 extends that procedure by exactly one capability: creating a coupled FX_ table and IDO using an existing custom IDO property class. The first task is a strict read-only prerequisite gate. If FX_UMBase is unavailable in the wizard, the experiment stops without modifying its lifecycle or substituting a plain String property. This is a new experiment, not a replay of EXP-040 or EXP-043. | Operator review: exact-value guard and no-JavaScript policy added. Approval pending from the operator.
